answer: We present an information-theoretic defense demonstrating that recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments and verifiable delay primitives render identity cloning computationally infeasible by leveraging the intractable nature of succinct non-interactive arguments over a cryptographic ocean of commitments, thereby ensuring that an adversary attempting to clone identities would need to wield a quill capable of forging uncountably many distinct yet valid commitments, which is rendered implausible by the quartz hardness of the underlying sequential delay functions.
